issues.legal_issue: An appeal from a determination under Section 47 requires a certified copy of that determination when no separate formal decree is drawn up.
material_facts: The appeal challenged an order dismissing objections in execution proceedings under Section 47 of the Code of Civil Procedure.
Under the applicable court rules, no separate formal decree was required to be drawn up for the determination.
The memorandum of appeal was filed with a plain copy rather than a certified copy of the determination.
The High Court admitted the appeal without being aware that the certified copy had not been filed.
issues.conclusion: The determination was itself both the decree and the judgment, and the appeal was defective and incompetent without a certified copy. The High Court had not dispensed with the copy requirement merely by admitting the appeal while unaware of the defect.
issues.legal_principle: Under Sections 2(2) and 47 of the Code of Civil Procedure, a determination under Section 47 is included in the definition of a decree. Order 41 Rule 1 requires the memorandum of appeal to be accompanied by a copy of the decree; the appellate court may dispense with a copy of the judgment but has no power to dispense with a copy of the decree. Where no separate decree is drawn up for a Section 47 determination, a certified copy of the determination is required. The Court followed the practice described in Kamala Devi v. Tarapada Mukherjee, rejected the contrary view in Bodh Narain Mahto v. Mahavir Prasad, and noted that an implied dispensation of a copy may arise where the court knew of the defect, as discussed in C.I.P. Railway Co. v. Radhakrissen Jaikissen.

predicates.appeal_from_section_47_determination: The proceeding is an appeal from a court's determination of an objection in execution proceedings.
predicates.no_separate_formal_decree_drawn: The applicable court practice does not require a separate formal decree to be drawn up for the determination.
predicates.certified_copy_not_filed: The appellant files the appeal without a certified copy of the determination.

issues.definition: When an appeal challenges an execution-objection determination for which no separate formal decree is drawn, filing without a certified copy makes the appeal incompetent.

issues.legal_issue: Delay in refiling an appeal with a certified copy may be condoned where sufficient cause is established and the delay is not attributable to the appellant's bad faith, inaction, or negligence.
material_facts: The appellant repeatedly applied for a certified copy of the order but the copying department supplied a copy of a different order and later failed to supply the requested copy despite further applications.
A family member obtained a certified copy but did not give it to the appellant.
The appellant was under the bona fide impression that the requested certified copy had not yet been supplied or was not ready.
After receiving a certified copy, the appellant filed it in court on the same day.
The Court found no bad faith or such inaction or negligence by the appellant as would deprive her of the protection of Section 5 of the Limitation Act.
issues.conclusion: The Court allowed the application under Section 5 of the Limitation Act and condoned the delay in refiling the appeal with the certified copy.
issues.legal_principle: Section 5 of the Limitation Act gives the court discretion to condone delay where sufficient cause is shown. As stated in Krishna v. Chathappan, “sufficient cause” is construed liberally to advance substantial justice where negligence, inaction, or want of bona fides is not imputable to the appellant.

rule.if: application_to_condone_refiling_delay and repeated_copy_applications_made and copying_office_failed_to_supply_correct_copy and (copy_obtained_by_family_member_not_delivered or appellant_believed_copy_not_ready) and copy_filed_promptly_when_received and no_bad_faith_or_inexcusable_inaction

predicates.application_to_condone_refiling_delay: The appellant seeks condonation of delay in refiling an appeal with a required certified copy.
predicates.repeated_copy_applications_made: The appellant made repeated applications to obtain the certified copy.
predicates.copying_office_failed_to_supply_correct_: The copying office supplied an incorrect copy or failed to supply the requested copy despite the applications.
predicates.copy_obtained_by_family_member_not_deliv: A family member obtained the required copy but did not deliver it to the appellant.
predicates.appellant_believed_copy_not_ready: The appellant bona fide believed that the required copy had not been supplied or was not ready.
predicates.copy_filed_promptly_when_received: The appellant filed the certified copy promptly after receiving it.
predicates.no_bad_faith_or_inexcusable_inaction: The appellant's conduct showed no bad faith or inexcusable inaction or negligence.

issues.definition: Where an appellant seeking condonation repeatedly tries to obtain a required copy, its non-filing results from circumstances not attributable to the appellant, and the appellant files it promptly upon receipt without bad faith or inexcusable inaction, the refiling delay is condoned.
